aboutUsText: We believe that culture builds bridges. Golestan Cultural Hub creates spaces where people can engage in meaningful conversations, share their stories, and develop new ideas together. Golestan Cultural Hub sees itself as a platform for intercultural exchange and cultural encounters. Inspired by the Persian word “Golestan,” meaning “garden of flowers,” we create a place where people from diverse cultural and social backgrounds can come together, share their experiences, and learn from one another.
homePageInfoBoxTextOne: This course introduces young people to a variety of creative forms of expression, including collage, photography, puppet making, filmmaking, and digital storytelling. Through hands-on activities and collaborative projects, participants develop creativity, media literacy, and teamwork skills in an engaging and supportive environment. At the end of the course, participants present their own creative projects to the group and the wider community.
homePageInfoBoxTextTwo: This course offers an introduction to the world of cinema, covering topics such as screenwriting, directing, visual storytelling, and film analysis. Through the discussion of selected films, participants explore social, cultural, and political issues while examining how films shape and reflect our understanding of the world. The course encourages critical thinking, media awareness, and a deeper appreciation of cinematic storytelling.
homePageInfoBoxTextThree: In this course, participants explore some of the most influential works of Persian literature, from Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh and Saadi’s Golestan to folk tales and contemporary literary works. Through reading, discussion, and creative activities, participants gain insight into Persian cultural heritage, storytelling traditions, and their continuing relevance in today’s world. The course promotes cultural understanding, literary appreciation, and intercultural dialogue.
HomepageMainWorkshopTitle: Family Collage Workshop: “Our City, Our Stories”
HomepageMainWorkshopText: In this creative family workshop, children and adults work together to create collages using recycled materials such as paper, fabric scraps, magazines, and packaging materials. Through images, colors, and textures, participants transform personal memories, cultural experiences, and ideas of community into unique works of art. The workshop encourages creativity, intergenerational collaboration, and sustainable practices while providing a space for families to share stories, express themselves, and explore the diversity of the communities in which they live.
HomepageMissionText: Our mission is to create a vibrant meeting place for cultural encounters and intercultural exchange. Through art, literature, music, workshops, and culinary experiences, we bring together people from diverse backgrounds and foster dialogue, mutual understanding, and active participation in society. As a space of diversity, creativity, and connection, we create opportunities for shared learning, personal growth, and cultural bridges between migrant communities and German society. At the same time, we provide families with a welcoming environment where cultural experiences can be enjoyed together across generations.
HomepageOurProgramsText: Golestan Cultural Hub offers a diverse range of cultural and artistic workshops, creative courses, and community-based events for people of different ages, backgrounds, and interests. At the heart of our program are art and painting workshops that explore drawing, illustration, collage, and experimental interdisciplinary art practices. These offerings are complemented by literature and creative writing workshops, where participants engage in storytelling, autobiographical writing, poetry sessions, and other forms of creative expression. In addition, music and performance programs—including small concerts, open stages, and rhythm and sound workshops—encourage cultural exchange and active creative participation. Craft and design workshops introduce both traditional and contemporary techniques, ranging from textile arts and handicrafts to sustainable design practices. A particular focus is placed on intergenerational activities for women, families, young people, and seniors, creating opportunities for meaningful encounters, collaborative learning, and creative engagement. These programs are further enriched by community-based projects such as exhibitions, readings, cultural markets, and festivals that bring people together and make cultural diversity visible, accessible, and enjoyable for all.

aboutus_founding_idea_description: Naghmeh Esmaeilpour founded Golestan Cultural Hub as a platform to promote cultural exchange and overcome barriers between different cultures. Her central motto is: "Culture is global and for all." The goal is to rethink integration through creative, practical participation instead of purely theoretical language learning. Refugees and migrants are encouraged to actively share their identity, talents, and cultural backgrounds.
aboutus_challenge_description: Golestan Cultural Hub sees itself as a platform for intercultural exchange and cultural encounters. Despite good language skills, many migrants and refugees still face barriers such as fear of rejection, discrimination, and lack of genuine participation. This leads to withdrawal and weak social connections. Integration remains one-sided and superficial instead of becoming a shared cultural process. At Golestan Cultural Hub, we aim to prevent the integration process from becoming a one-way road and instead focus on building bridges that connect different nations and cultures equally. Through art, literature, music, workshops, and culinary experiences, we foster dialogue between migrant communities and German society.
aboutus_goal_description: Inspired by the Persian word “Golestan,” meaning “garden of flowers,” Golestan Cultural Hub creates a place where people from diverse cultural and social backgrounds can come together, share their experiences, and learn from one another. Golestan's focus is not on deficits or assimilation, but on cultural identity as a shared resource. Through art, literature, music, workshops, and culinary experiences, we foster dialogue between migrant communities and German society. Like Saadi’s famous Golestan, our Cultural Hub aims to be a space that invites people to listen, tell stories, reflect, and grow together.

team_members_meet_people: Meet the People Behind the Mission
team_members_description: Our team brings together educators, researchers, and cultural practitioners dedicated to sharing the rich history, traditions, and contemporary cultures of the Middle East.
team_members_naghmeh_description: Naghmeh Esmaeilpour finished her PhD in 2021 in “General and Comparative Literature” in 2021 at Humboldt University, Germany with a scholarship from Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung, and her BA and MA in English Language and Literature from Islamic Azad University, Karaj, Iran. She presented different papers in conferences mostly held in Germany. She was a visiting scholar at Cambridge University in 2019 and at Harvard University in 2016. She was also a colloquium leader at IWL (Harvard Institute of World Literature) summer school in 2021. She has published several articles, namely, “Globalization in Pre- and Post-revolutionary Iranian Literature” in Bloomsbury World Literature Series and “Transmedial Histography in Videogames, Representation of Iran (Iranians) in Games” in U.S. American Culture as Popular Culture. Her monograph, Interactions between Iranian and American Literatures: Strange Affinity, is a published by Routledge in 2024. Her research areas are comparative literature, (global) media culture, trans-intermediality, film, game, and narrative studies.
team_members_naghmeh_interests: Comparative studies, particularly Iranian and American literature and film
Development of educational and cultural initiatives
team_members_pegah_khadish_description: Pegah Khadish has completed training in Persian language and literature. She completed her PhD at the University of Tehran (2005). Her doctoral thesis was on the morphology of Persian folk tales, which was written under the supervision of Prof. Ulrich Marzloph at the University of Göttingen. This dissertation was published in 2008 and was selected as the top cultural research of the year in Iran. She worked as an assistant professor for about 15 years at the Dehkhoda Lexicon Institute and the International Center for Persian Studies at the University of Tehran. Her main research area is Iranian myths and narratives. She has published nine books so far, most of them on Persian folk literature and narrative elements, two of which are considered textbooks. She has been a member of the ISFNR (The International Society for Folk Narrative Research) since 2017. She is currently working on a voluntary basis on cataloging some unknown Persian manuscripts in the Berlin State Library.
team_members_sanaz_pahlevan_description: Sanaz Pahlavi was born in November 1982. She initially studied family psychology and later earned a bachelor's degree in primary school teaching. During her studies, she developed a strong interest in crafts such as doll making, origami, collage, and embroidery (on fabric and leather). Believing in teaching children concepts through art and crafts, she obtained certifications from practical craft schools. She worked as a primary school teacher in Iran for approximately six years, teaching children theater and small decorative crafts for about three years. Later, after immigrating to Germany, she used her talent to teach third-grade children how to make decorative crafts for their families as Christmas gifts at school. Through KulturAtelier, I host a virtual workshop on small decorative crafts, which was well-received by 10 participants, despite being virtual due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
team_members_zhaleh_ahmadi_iraei_descrip: Zhaleh Ahmadi Iraei traditional and folk Iranian singer since 2011,collaborated with various music groups and contributed to multiple albums. In 2018, founded and led the Aysham group, earning top honors at the Lilim Folk Music Festival and representing Mazandaran at the Fajr Festival Setar Player, and children’s music teacher, Live in Germany since 2022, collaborating with Romak group. performed many concerts in Germany such as Open Cottbus Festival, Nowruz celebrations at Brandenburg University,Yalda Night in Vienna, Austria, Yalda night concerts at Cottbus university and VHS Pankow Berlin, Cultural concert at Stadtteilzentrum in Kiez Treff Berlin.YaldaNight at UNESCO Hall with Shewar Band in Paris, YaldaNight in Berlin 2020.
team_members_mahdi_gholi_zadeh_descripti: Mahdi Gholi Zadeh (born in 1979 in Amol, Iran) is an outstanding multi-percussionist, teacher, and musician who has been living in Germany since 2022. Although he holds a degree in IT engineering, he discovered his lifelong passion for music at a young age, having grown up in a family of musicians. He gained his first musical experience with Middle Eastern percussion instruments such as the daf, tombak, and darbuka. From 2000 to 2005, Mahdi formally studied Latin American percussion, focusing on instruments such as congas, bongos, cajón, and djembe. His constant curiosity about rhythm led him to learn the Indian instrument tabla in 2013. In 2014, he began taking advanced master classes, where he refined his skills on congas and bongos as well as in a variety of global techniques and styles, such as Afro-Cuban, Afro-Brazilian, and timbales. He also mastered smaller percussion instruments such as shakers, cabassa, and maracas, with a strong focus on world grooves and ensemble playing. He continued this professional training through 2018. Mahdi’s professional career began in 1997 and spans more than two decades. He has performed both as a soloist and as an ensemble musician in various genres—including folk, pop, flamenco, and classical music—and has collaborated with the Philharmonic Orchestra as well as on numerous music projects and albums since 2002. Since 2002, he has devoted himself with great passion to teaching, instructing rhythm and percussion at various institutions for children, teenagers, and adults. Between 2015 and 2021, he was In 2019, he published a book about the desarketen, a traditional percussion instrument from the Mazandaran region. The book documents its history and includes an educational repertoire aimed at preserving the Iranian folk music tradition. Today, Mahdi teaches percussion at the Berlin Musikschule Zehlendorf and performs with two ensembles: the Just Mad Big Band and a Latin band. He is also the founder and director of the Romak Music Band, which, together with singer Zhaleh Ahmadi, has given numerous concerts in various cities across Germany and Austria. Mahdi Gholi Zadeh’s remarkable career as a musician and educator reflects his lifelong dedication to rhythm, cultural exchange, and the art of percussion.
team_members_mitra_nasayehi_description: Mitra Nasayehi earned her bachelor’s degree in graphic design and subsequently began her professional career as a graphic designer. She worked for two years at an advertising agency and later founded her own advertising agency to work as a freelancer and pursue her interest in painting and drawing. To cultivate her interest in the arts, she studied painting and drawing at the university for about two years. Drawing on her experience as a graphic designer, she began her career as a painter and draftsman. She has painted and sold many works of art to date and continued her work after immigrating. She believes that people can express their feelings, emotions, and view of the world through art and artistic creation, particularly through painting. This will help them overcome their problems by calming their minds. I would like to share my experiences through painting and drawing workshops at the KulturAtelier for both young people and adults.
team_members_mohamad_tavakoli_targhi_rol: History Nights: Critical Re-Readings of Historical and Political Narratives in Contemporary Iran
team_members_mohamad_tavakoli_targhi_des: Mohamad Tavakoli-Targhi is Professor of History and Near and Middle Eastern Civilizations at the University of Toronto. His areas of specialization encompass Middle Eastern History, Modernity, Nationalism, Gender Studies, Orientalism, and Occidentalism. He is the author of two books, Refashioning Iran: Orientalism, Occidentalism and Nationalist Historiography (Palgrave, 2001) and Tajaddud-i Bumi [Vernacular Modernity] (in Persian, Nashr-i Tarikh, 2003). He has authored numerous articles.
team_members_asef_bayat_role: History Nights: Critical Re-Readings of Historical and Political Narratives in Contemporary Iran
team_members_asef_bayat_description: Asef Bayat is professor of sociology, and Catherine and Bruce Bastian Professor of Global and Transnational Studies at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign. His research areas range from social movements and social change, to religion and public life, urban space and politics, and contemporary Middle Eastern societies. His latest books include „Global Middle East: Into the 21st Century“ (ed. With Linda Herrera) (University of California Press, 2021), and „Revolutionary Life: The Everyday of the Arab Spring“ (Harvard University Press, 2021).
